method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the 'Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)' chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the Stroke Foundation, Kidney Health Australia and NHFA/CSANZ sources already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Infants: 4 doses at 2, 4, 6 and 18 months.** The **first can be as early as 6 weeks**; if so, the next doses stay at **4 and 6 months**.
claims.source_text: Hib-containing vaccine is recommended in a 4-dose schedule for infants at 2, 4, 6 and 18 months of age. Infants can have their 1st dose as early as 6 weeks of age. If the 1st dose is given at 6 weeks of age, infants should still receive their next scheduled doses at 4 months and 6 months of age.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/haemophilus-influenzae-type-b-hib, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Children under 5 who missed a dose** should catch up.
claims.source_text: infants and children <5 years of age who have missed a dose of Hib-containing vaccine
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/haemophilus-influenzae-type-b-hib, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Asplenia (functional or anatomical): 1 dose of Hib.** ⚠️ **Haematopoietic stem cell transplant: 3 doses, starting 6 months after the transplant.**
claims.source_text: People who have functional or anatomical asplenia are recommended to receive 1 dose of Hib vaccine. People who have received a haematopoietic stem cell transplant are recommended to receive 3 doses of Hib vaccine commencing from 6 months after the transplant.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/haemophilus-influenzae-type-b-hib, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Hib causes invasive disease including **epiglottitis, septic arthritis and cellulitis**.
